introduction:
In Uttar Pradesh, the Jati Praman Patra (Caste Certificate) is issued by the District Magistrate (DM) / Tehsildar / Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) for SC, ST, and OBC applicants. It is an essential document to claim reservations in education, government jobs, and welfare benefits.

UP citizens can apply online through the e-Sathi Portal (esathi.up.gov.in) or offline at the nearest Tehsil / CSC centre. The certificate is based on the ancestral permanent residential address in Uttar Pradesh.
quickFacts:
Important Quick Facts
  • Service Name: Caste Certificate (Jati Praman Patra). Available in Hindi (valid for UP State-level use) or English (valid for Central Government use).
  • State: Uttar Pradesh
  • Target Audience: CSC (Common Service Center) Operators / Jan Seva Kendra Operators.
  • Official Portal: UP e-District (edistrict.up.gov.in).
  • Processing Time: Generally 5 to 7 days, occasionally 10 to 12 days. The official maximum limit is 20 working days.
  • Mandatory e-KYC: Aadhaar e-KYC (OTP verification) is mandatory.
  • Upload Constraint: Every uploaded document must be strictly under 100 KB in size, or the upload will fail.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: All files must be compressed to strictly under 100 KB before uploading.
Applicant Documents
  • Aadhaar Card: Scanned copy of the applicant's Aadhaar.
  • Applicant's Photograph: Passport-size photo (Alternatively, the operator can fetch the photo directly from the applicant's Aadhaar database).
  • Self-Declaration Form (Swa-Pramanit Ghoshna Patra): A standard form downloaded from the portal, filled and signed by the applicant.
Supporting Evidences
  • Verification Letter: Written report/letter from the Gram Pradhan (for rural areas) or Parshad (for urban areas) verifying the applicant's caste.
  • Old Caste Certificate: If available, it should be attached as supporting evidence.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Online Application (For CSC / Jan Seva Kendra Operators)

This application must be filed online through the official e-District portal using operator credentials. General citizens cannot apply directly here.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Login): Go to the e-District UP website (edistrict.up.gov.in). Click "e-District Login", select "CSC/e-District User" from the dropdown, and log in with your CSC ID, password, and captcha. (Tip: If you get an "Access Denied" error, click "Logout Everywhere" and log in again).
  2. Step 2 (Select Service): Under the certificates section on the dashboard, click on "Jati Praman Patra (Hindi)" or "Jati Praman Patra (Angrezi)".
  3. Step 3 (Aadhaar e-KYC): Enter the applicant's Aadhaar number and captcha. Submit it to send an OTP to the applicant's Aadhaar-linked mobile number. Enter the OTP to open the main form.
  4. Step 4 (Applicant Details): Select Rural (Gramin) or Urban (Nagariya). The applicant's name in Hindi and English auto-populates from Aadhaar. Fill in the Father's/Husband's/Guardian's name, Mother's name, full address, and mobile number.
  5. Step 5 (Caste Details): Select the Category (e.g., Backward Class, SC, ST) and then select the specific Sub-Caste from the dropdown list.
  6. Step 6 (Additional Info): Enter the reason for applying (e.g., "Sarkari Karya Hetu" - For government work). Select "Yes" or "No" depending on whether a certificate was issued previously.
  7. Step 7 (Upload Documents): From the dropdown, select the document type (Photo, Self-Declaration, Pradhan Letter, Aadhaar, etc.) and browse your computer to upload each file (max 100 KB each).
  8. Step 8 (Review & Submit): Enter the security code and click "Darj Kare" (Submit). Check the preview. Click "Avedan Sanshodhit Kare" (Edit) if changes are needed, otherwise click "Darj Kare" again.
  9. Step 9 (Payment): You will be redirected to the CSC wallet gateway (e.g., Vayamtech). Enter your wallet credentials to pay the service fee.
  10. Step 10 (Final Approval Routing): Click "Proceed Forward to Approval Authority" to route the application to the concerned officer. Print the generated Acknowledgement Slip (Pavati).
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Offline Application (Direct Citizen Route)

If citizens want to apply directly without visiting a CSC kiosk, they can follow the physical offline route at local government offices.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1 (Visit Office): Visit your local Tehsil office, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office, or Revenue Department.
  2. Step 2 (Get Form): Request the physical Caste Certificate application form.
  3. Step 3 (Fill Details): Fill out the form meticulously with personal, address, and caste details.
  4. Step 4 (Attach Documents): Attach self-attested copies of Aadhaar, Ration card, Self-Declaration form, Gram Pradhan/Parshad verification letter, and passport-size photographs.
  5. Step 5 (Submit): Submit the application folder to the concerned counter or to the local Lekhpal.
  6. Step 6 (Field Enquiry & Issue): The Lekhpal will conduct a field inquiry to verify your caste eligibility. Once verified, the Tehsildar will issue the Caste Certificate.
afterApplying:
After Applying — Verification & Issuance

1. Verification Flow

The submitted application is routed to the local Lekhpal (Revenue Officer) for field verification.

2. Processing Time

The expected disposal date is usually 20 working days. Typically, verification and Tehsildar approval take 5 to 7 days if documents are correct.

3. Download & Collection

Once approved, the digitally signed certificate is delivered to the CSC operator's e-District inbox. The operator can download, print, and hand it over to the applicant.
